Title: Garment Animation Making
Content: Objective Tips for creating stable and realistic garment animation for multi-layered garments. Operation Optimize 3D Garment for Animation The heavier the garment, the slower and harder it records. Follow the steps below to make it lighter. For a multi-layered garment, increase particle distance to 20mm for inner layers that are not as visible as outer layers. Delete invisible and any other unnecessary layers. Outer layers: Set the particle distance to 10mm for parts that does not require higher level of expression of wrinkles. Set the particle distance to 5mm for parts that require higher level of expression of wrinkles. If there is large quantity of layers set to 5mm, set all of them to 7mm. Fix Garment If garment is not fixed to avatar while recording the animation, the garment moves drastically around the avatar due to collision. Certain parts of the garment need to be fixed to the avatar or itself to create more realistic recording. Use functions such as 'Avatar Tape' or 'Tack on Avatar' to attach shoulder and sides of the garment. Use 'Tack' function for overlapped layers or any parts that may dangle. Increase Transition Animation Time Increase the transition animation time for heavier garments. In the animation dialogue, enter 5FPS to stabilize the simulation. This makes the avatar movement slower which helps to minimize the collision between the garments. Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for the First Recording Setting Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' minimizes the collision between the avatar and garments. To save time, the simulation quality can be set to 'Normal' for the middle part of the recording as the avatar and garments tend to collide more in the beginning and end. Make sure the simulation to set the quality back on 'Complete' for the end of the Transition Animation. Reevaluate Draping of the Garment after the Recording As the avatar moves, some parts of the garment may collide. When the simulation is off, the 3D garment may appear fine, however there is possibility of unnoticeable collision which may destabilize rest of the recording. Return to Simulation Mode. Note: From ver2.5.0, it is possible to simulate by pressing the Simulation button without recording it. Active simulation and make sure the entire garment simulation is stable. If any parts of the garment is unstable, readjust the layers by using the Select/Move tool. Once the simulation has been stabilized, go back to the Animation Mode. Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' when Recording the Actual Garment Animation Make sure to set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for final recordings of Garment Animation as the 'Complete' and the 'Normal' give clearly different results in expressing reality.

Title: Record Animation
Content: Objective Record garment animation. Note: Follow the link Process of Making Garment Animation for your reference on creating garment animation in details. Location Animation Mode Animation Editor Record Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Animation Mode Animation Editor Record Simulation turns on automatically and it is now being recorded in frames. If a Transition Animation is created, the recording automatically stops at the end of the Transition Animation frame and starts again (ver2.5.0). Note: Transition Animation is auto-generated animation tool which automatically generates for stabilizing transition when the original Avatar pose is different to the first pose in the motion file. Once the garment and avatar arrive in a new position, it is no longer in need therefore the recording automatically stops for you to delete this unnecessary part. Once the Avatar's motion ends, the recording automatically stops. To stop the recording while it is in process, click the Pause button.

Title: Fold Seam Line
Content: Objective Use this function to create an pressing effect on sewn parts of Patterns. Location Pattern Property Editor Fold Fold Angle Operation Click on Edit Sewing tool. Select the seamline to change its fold angle. Follow the indicated guideline below: Pattern Property Editor Fold Fold Angle Adjust the value, in the range of 0~360. Note: The value of fold angle is in between 0 to 360, 180 represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360. Fold Strength The intensity of the fold is able to be set by adjusting the value of Fold Strength. The higher the value, the closer the fold is to the set angle. When a jacket and its lining are sewn together, the sewn area inflates due to the default sewing angle and intensity values. In this case, sets the Fold Strength to 0 to flatten the sewn boundaries. When the Sewing type is set as Turned, Fold Strength and Fold Angle cannot be modified (ver4.0.0).

Title: Select Mesh & Apply to Selected Meshes
Content: List of Contents Select Mesh (Brush) / (Lasso) / (Box) Apply to Selected Meshes Objective Select some meshes of 3D garment or apply Subdivided, Freeze, Solidify, Solidify to selected meshes. Watch tutorial video here. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select Mesh (Brush) / (Box) / (Lasso) 3D Toolbar (Click for more than 2 seconds) Select Mesh (Brush) / (Box) / (Lasso) Operation Select Mesh (Brush) / (Box) / (Lasso) Select the tool/ menu indicated. Click and drag the desired area on a garment. The area is selected. Note: Select Mesh (Brush) - Set Strength, Size, and Focal in the Brush window at the top-right corner. Select Mesh (Lasso) / (Box) - To select meshes additionally, press Shift+Ctrl on the keyboard then click and drag on the garment. To deselect the selected area, press Ctrl and click and drag on the garment. Select Mesh (Lasso) / (Box) - Double click a Pattern outline/ internal line in either the 3D/ 2D window to select Mesh along the segment. When selecting Mesh on the Pattern, adjacent segment vertices are also selected. Subdivide / Freeze / Solidify (ver 6.1) / Strengthen (ver 7.1) Select the tool/ menu indicated. Right-click on the selected meshes and select the menu Subdivide / Freeze / Solidify (ver 6.1) / Strengthen (ver 7.1). Each menu is applied to the meshes and displayed in different colors. Set the properties of the applied options in the property editor. Subdivide(Mesh) Name Name the subdivided mesh area. Level Set the subdivision level of mesh. The higher the value is, the smaller the mesh is. Smooth Subdivide the area between the subdivided area and the normal area progressively. Solidify/Strengthen Strength Set the intensity of Solidify and Strengthen. To apply the desired option, right click the mesh area that each option is applied to. Note: Right-click an empty area in the 3D window and click the Show/ Hide Color menu to hide each color of the mesh areas.

Title: Edit Simulation Properties
Content: Objective Configure the simulation properties for advanced scene settings. Location Object Browser Scene Environment Simulation Properties Operation Select the tool/menu indicated. The simulation properties appear in the Property Editor. Refer to the below table and edit the simulation properties as needed. Option Description Preset Instead of selecting the simulation mode from the 3D toolbar, you can choose predefined presets here. Normal, Fitting, and GPU simulations are primarily used. Time Step This determines the time values calculated within the simulation engine. The smaller you set it, the more sophisticated it will be, but it will also require more calculations and will, resultingly, be slower. The default values are recommended. Number of Simulation When calculating cloth simulation for a given time step, this denotes how many substeps one simulation calculation is divided into. For example, if you are calculating a time step of 0.03 and number of simulation is 10, the actual time step will be 0.003. Simulating multiple times with these smaller time intervals ensures both more numerically accurate results and stable collision handling, but takes much longer. CG Finish Condition, CG Iteration Count, CG Residual Clothing simulation is the process of solving a large linear system. Large linear systems can be solved using a numerical analysis method called conjugate gradient method (CG). CG improves the accuracy of the answer through iterative calculations. The condition for CG ending can be set by the number of iterations or when the error (=residual) falls below a certain value. Iteration: Because it repeats only a certain number of times and ends unconditionally, it is faster but may be less accurate. Residual: It is slower but can be more accurate because it stops when the error falls below a certain value. Self Collision Iteration Count Defines the number of collision calculations for the clothing. More collision calculations produce more precise results, but they are also slower. Please use the default value. Air Damping The resistance that the garment receives from the air. Gravity Defines the most important gravity values in your simulation. If this value is adjusted, simulation results will become unrealistic. Please use the default value, unless you want to, for example, create a weightless simulation. Number of CPU in Use This determines the number of physical cores within the CPU that will be used for the simulation. CLO can technically use up to 12 cores, which are automatically defined based on your computer. Even if it is a high-end CPU with 16 cores, up to 12 can be used. This may vary depending on the CPU manufacturer and actual CPU products. This value is best also left at default. Nonlinear Simulation Linear or non-linear is an important factor in all fields of computer graphics, simulation, rendering and engineering. By analogy, the real world is non-linear, but computer implementations are linear. Nonlinearity is a technique that makes things look very real, and simulating them this way is sophisticated, but slow. If Fitting simulation is run, this option is selected. t's slower because it's more complicated and requires a lot of calculations. Ground, Avatar-Cloth Collision Detection, Self-Collision Detection, Proximity Detection All of these are intended to simulate collisions and friction between the clothing and the avatar. Because CLO calculates numerous contacts and collisions between the fabric and the body, the simulation looks natural and realistic. It is recommended that these values are also left at their default. Note: Use the Open &amp Save buttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the settings.

Title: Select/Move Button
Content: List of Contents Select/Move Button Moving Buttons Moving Buttonholes Rotating Buttons/Buttonholes Adjusting Thread Length Editing Buttonhole Bind Position Changing Button/Buttonhole Item Button Collision Select/Move Button - Select or move buttons or buttonholes in the 2D and the 3D Window. - Choose the Select/Move Button tool from the 3D Window. Moving Buttons 3D Window - Choose the Select/Move Button tool from the 3D Window. - Navigate to the 3D Window. Then, click and drag the button to be moved. - To easily and precisely move or rotate the button, click on the button to access the Gizmo tool. - Click and drag green arrow to move the button vertically click and drag red arrow to move the button horizontally. - Click the blue arrow and drag downwards to pull the button forwards click the blue arrow and drag upwards to push the button backwards. - Click and drag the yellow box to move the button freely. - Click and drag the green circle to rotate the button in X-axis click and drag the red circle to rotate the button in Y-axis. - Click and drag the blue circle clockwise or counterclockwise to rotate the button respectively. 2D Window - Choose the Select/Move Button tool from the 3D Window and navigate to the 2D Window. - Click and drag the button to be moved. - To move the button with specific values, click and drag the button, and then while holding down the left button of the mouse, right click once. - When the Moving Distance Window appears, enter the desired values in Distance Moved or Position to designate the location. Moving Buttonholes - Choose the Select/Move Button tool from the 3D Window. - Navigate to the 2D or the 3D Window to select the buttonhole to be moved. - Click and drag to move the buttonhole freely. - In the 2D Window, right click while moving the buttonhole to access the Moving Distance Window. - When the Moving Distance Window appears, enter the desired values in Distance Moved or Position to designate the location. Rotating Buttons/Buttonholes Button - With the Select/Move Button tool selected, click on the button to be rotated. - The selected buttons property will appear in the Property Editor. - Enter the desired value in Angle to rotate the button. - Or, click on the button in the 3D Window. Then, rotate the button using the Gizmo tool. Buttonhole - With the Select/Move Button tool selected, click on the buttonhole to be rotated. - The selected buttonholes property will appear in the Property Editor. - Enter the desired value in Angle to rotate the buttonhole. Adjusting Thread Length - With the Select/Move Button tool selected, click on the button to be edited. - In the Property Editor, the selected buttons property will appear. - Enter the desired value in Thread Length to adjust the offset distance between the button and the 3D garment. Editing Buttonhole Bind Position - With the Select/Move Button tool selected, click on the buttonhole to be edited. - In the Property Editor, the selected buttonholes property will appear. - Adjust Bind Position to decide on which edge of the buttonhole the button will be fastened to. Changing Button/Buttonhole Item Button Item - With the Select/Move Button tool selected, click on the button to be edited. - In the Property Editor, the selected buttons property will appear. - Expand the Style drop down menu and choose desired button item. Buttonhole Item - With the Select/Move Button tool selected, click on the buttonhole to be edited. - In the Property Editor, the selected buttonholes property will appear. - Expand the Style drop down menu and choose desired buttonhole item. Button Collision - With the Select/Move Button tool selected, click on the button to be edited. - In the Property Editor, the selected buttons property will appear. - Toggle on/off Collision. - When Collision is turned off, the selected button will not be calculated for collision and be fixed at the location that the button was created.

Title: Show 2D Sewing
Content: Show 2D Sewing - Show Sewing Lines at your convenience even while not using the Sewing tools. - Select the Show 2D Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Display Show 2D Sewing - When the Show 2D Sewing tool is activated, the Sewing Lines will show or hide from the 2D window.

Title: Elastic
Content: List of Contents Elastic Applicable Items Apply Elastic Simulation Elastic Strength Elastic Ratio Segment Length Total Length Elastic - Apply Elastic to Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to shrink or stretch 3D Patterns. - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and select the Pattern outline or the Internal Line as desired. Then, navigate to the Property Editor and toggle on Elastic. Applicable Items - Elastic can be applied to all Pattern outlines. - Elastic can be applied to all Internal Lines. Apply Elastic - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and select the segment where Elastic should be applied to. - Elastic can also be applied to a whole Pattern by selecting it with the Transform Pattern tool. - Once the desired item is selected, navigate to the Property Editor and toggle on Elastic. - Elastic will be applied to the selected items. Simulation - Select the Simulation tool from the 3D toolbar. - The elastic will be applied to 3D Garments. Elastic Strength - Elastic Strength refers to the Elastic resistance. - The default value is 10. Greater the Elastic Strength is, lesser affected by outside influence and maintain Elastic Ratio. - It is recommended to set the Elastic Strength to 10. Elastic Ratio - Elastic Ratio indicates by what percentage the selected Pattern outlines or Internal Lines will shrink or stretch. - 100% is the original length of the selected Pattern outlines or Internal Lines. Smaller the percentage is, shorter the length is. - The Elastic Ratio can be adjusted between 0 and 200. Segment Length - Type in the desired segment length of the selected Pattern outlines or Internal Lines after the Elastic is applied. - The Elastic Ratio will be automatically calculated when the Segment Length is assigned. Total Length - Select multiple segments and type in the desired length for the sum of selected segments.

Title: Dart
Content: List of Contents Dart Create Dart Create Dart with Specific Values Dart - Create Dart on Patterns. Because Patterns can be sewn without seam allowances in CLO, Dart will be sewn with the Pattern outlines. - Select the Dart tool from the 2D toolbar or navigate to and select Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Dart. Create Dart - Select the Dart tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window and click and drag within a Pattern. - The preview of the Dart will appear. - Release the mouse to complete the Dart. Create Dart with Specific Values - Select the Dart tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window and click once within a Pattern. - The Create Dart window will appear. - Enter desired values to the Create Dart window and select OK. Size - Assign Width (Left), Width (Right), Height (Up), and Height (Down) which are measured from the center of the Dart. Position - Assign the placement of the Dart. Outline - Enter Left, Right, Up, and Down values which indicate the margin between the Dart and the Pattern outline. Center - Enter Left, Right, Up, and Down values which are measured from the center of the Dart

Title: Create Smooth Curve
Content: Objective Modify Pattern outlines or Internal Lines into smooth curves. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar Smooth Curve Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar Smooth Curve Click on a segment or point to establish the first point. The point appears in grey. Drag the mouse. A grey arrow extending from the point follows the cursor. Click on another segment or point to establish the endpoint. A reference line is created between the two points. With the reference line created, click on the side that will be converted into a smooth curve. The entire side is highlighted in yellow. Click &amp drag the reference line to create the desired smooth curve. The entire outline of the selected side is replaced by the reference line. 참조: Cancel Actions Cancel All Actions While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Esc or Ctrl+Z on the keyboard and all actions are undone. Cancel Last Action While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Delete or Backspace on the keyboard and the last action is undone.

Title: [Popup] Copy/Paste Buttonhole
Content: List of Contents Copy/Paste Buttonhole Input Interval/Number/Position to Copy/Paste Buttonhole Objective Copy and paste multiple buttonholes with keeping the interval space evenly. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Copy/Paste Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on an existing buttonhole, then select Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V) from the pop-up menu. Click on a desired place to locate the copy of the buttonhole. Input Interval/Number/Position to Copy/Pase Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on an existing buttonhole, then select Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V) from the pop-up menu. Right click on a desired place to locate the copy of the buttonhole. The Paste window appears. Input desired value for interval/number of buttonholes/position. Interval Sets the distance between buttonholes. Number of Buttons/Buttonholes Sets the number of buttonholes to copy/paste. Position Sets the position of the center of the copied button/buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline (ver2.5.0). Click OK. The buttonholes are now being created and applied accordingly.
